suggested_experiment_name: Neutron Star Cooling (Cas A and NS1987A)
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing parameter χ (dimensionless), as plotted on y-axis labeled 'ε'
notes: Paper derives constraints on dark photons and U(1)_{B-L} gauge bosons from cooling of young neutron stars Cassiopeia A and SN1987A. For dark photons: εm_γ' < 1.5 × 10^-8 MeV for m_γ' < O(0.1) MeV from Cas A (Eq. 37); εm_γ' < 3 × 10^-9 MeV from NS1987A (Eq. 39). The constraint is mass-independent below the critical temperature T_c(n3P2) ~ 0.1 MeV, encoded as horizontal line. For U(1)_{B-L}: e' < 5 × 10^-13 (dimensionless coupling) from Cas A for m_γ' < 0.1 MeV. Paper also discusses hint for U(1)_{B-L} with m ~ eV and e' ~ 10^-13. Extraction confidence reflects clear numerical bounds in text but some model dependence on neutron triplet gap profile and envelope composition (η parameter). | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 29)) | Vision: Traced the lower boundary of the red Cas A exclusion region from FIG. 6 (dark photon scenario). The x-axis spans from 10^-2 to 10^8 eV (mass of dark photon m_γ'), and the y-axis spans from 10^-15 to 10^-7 (kinetic mixing ε). The boundary shows a characteristic rise from ~10^-11 at low masses (0.01 eV) to ~10^-6 at high masses (10^8 eV), with steeper slope above ~100 eV. The excluded region (red) lies ABOVE this boundary. Sampled more densely in the transition region (10-1000 eV) where the slope changes. The plot also shows constraints from NS1987A (tan region) and other astrophysical bounds (gray regions). The coupling convention is the standard kinetic mixing parameter χ, labeled as 'ε' on the plot. | Calibration: No calibration needed
